label: Sort each artifact by fidelity stage
prompt: Classify each design artifact as the stage of the fidelity spectrum it belongs to.

items.task: Hand-drawn boxes on a napkin during a coffee meeting
items.explanation: Fast, disposable, and meant to explore several layout ideas before committing to any one of them — the cheapest possible stage to be wrong at.

items.task: Grayscale boxes with placeholder text showing a header, sidebar, and content area
items.explanation: Real structure and content hierarchy, but no color, imagery, or finished copy yet — exactly what a low-fidelity wireframe is for.

items.task: The finished login screen with brand colors, the real logo, and finished button copy
items.explanation: Fully styled and realistic, but still a static image — nothing on it actually responds to a click yet.

items.task: A clickable Figma file that simulates the full checkout flow from cart to confirmation
items.explanation: Multiple mockups linked together so someone can click through a real flow — the last stop before code.

items.task: A whiteboard photo from a team meeting, redrawn three different ways
items.explanation: Cheap, fast iteration on layout ideas — the entire point of the sketch stage is producing (and discarding) several of these quickly.

items.task: A single static image showing the exact fonts, spacing, and photography for the homepage
items.explanation: Full visual design on one screen, but it's still just an image — no interaction, which is what separates a mockup from a prototype.
